steps.title: Summer 2008: trade at a record
text: In July 2008 the world's economies exported about **$1.6 trillion** of goods in a single month. No month would be higher until March 2011.

Trouble had already started: the [US](USA) economy entered recession in December 2007, and losses on mortgage-related assets were straining financial markets. But trade was still booming, helped by high commodity prices.

steps.title: September 2008: Lehman Brothers fails
text: In September 2008 the investment bank Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy, and the financial crisis went global.
The map now shows the change from the same month a year earlier. In September, world exports were still about **19% higher** than in September 2007, so most of the map is green.

steps.title: The free fall
text: Within a few months the map turns orange. By February 2009 world exports were **33% lower** than a year earlier, and the drop reached about **36%** in April 2009.
These are values in US dollars, which also fell because prices, especially oil, dropped. Measured by volume, the WTO put the 2009 decline at 12.2%, the largest since the Second World War.

ask.q: At the worst point, how far below a year earlier did world exports fall?

steps.title: Manufacturing exporters hit hardest
text: Countries that sell cars, machinery and electronics saw orders vanish. [Japan](JPN)'s exports in February 2009 were **41% lower** than a year earlier, and fell 44% by March.
[Germany](DEU)'s exports were down about a third (**−34%** in February). Hover over a partner to see how each market shrank.

steps.title: Oil exporters: the steepest drop
text: The price of oil collapsed from its mid-2008 peak, and with it the export earnings of oil producers.
Exports from the [Gulf Cooperation Council](GCC) states to the rest of the world were **56% lower** in May 2009 than a year earlier. [Russia](RUS)'s were about half (**−50%**).

steps.title: China and the United States
text: [China](CHN)'s exports fell less steeply, by about a quarter at the worst point (**−26%** in May 2009).
Its biggest single customer cut back sharply: [US](USA) imports from all countries were **36% lower** in May 2009 than a year earlier. The panel compares China's trade with the US over time.

steps.title: Rescue and rebound
text: In April 2009, G20 leaders meeting in London pledged **$250 billion** of support for trade finance as part of a wider rescue package. The [US](USA) recession officially ended in June 2009.
Trade bottomed out in the first half of 2009. By November 2009 world exports were above their level a year earlier again (+6%), partly because the end of 2008 was already depressed.

steps.title: The long view
text: In annual terms, world goods exports fell from **$16.3 trillion** in 2008 to **$12.4 trillion** in 2009 (−24%). They recovered to $15.3 trillion in 2010 and passed the 2008 level in 2011 ($18.3 trillion).
Press ▶ or drag the slider to see how trade developed after the crisis, or pick any country to explore its own story.
